_: Inputs to Tools/normalise_weapons.py. This file is NOT read at play time -- see Docs/HeldAssetStandard.md. Its whole job is to tell the bake how to turn a Synty mesh into HAC1 grip space, after which the game attaches weapons to the WeaponGrip_R socket with an identity transform and reads nothing from here.
_axis_hints: Which bounding-box axis becomes forward and which becomes up. 'long' is the longest extent, 'thin' the shortest, 'wide' the remaining one. up_sign settles the one thing geometry cannot: +1 keeps the measured up axis pointing the way it already does, -1 flips it. forward_sign likewise, where 'auto' means 'toward whichever end of the axis reaches further from the origin'.
_grip_rule: Where the hand closes, as a signed fraction of a measured bound, in the mesh's space AFTER the axes are fixed. ["min", 0.40] means 0.40 * bounds.min (a negative number, so this moves back toward the stock); ["min", -0.55] means the same distance FORWARD of the origin, which is how a blade's handle is expressed. "zero" pins the axis to the origin the artist already chose.
_overrides: Per weapon, keyed by catalogue key, for the ones the rules get wrong. An override may set any of forward/up/up_sign (strings and numbers as in axis_hints), extra_rot [pitch, yaw, roll] applied after normalisation, and extra_loc [x, y, z] in centimetres added to the grip point. Re-run Tools/normalise_weapons.py after editing; meshes already stamped hac1 are re-baked only when listed in force.
